body:
7,341 lead-form submissions. Nine Meta ad accounts. India, UK, US, Canada.

Every one of those numbers can be traced back to a screenshot, a report, or an ad account login.

That habit sounds small. It is the one thing that separates a number you can trust from a number someone just typed into a slide.

Here is what it means in practice. A lead count in a report should link to the actual Meta Ads Manager screen it came from — not a summary someone wrote a week later.

Say a manufacturer gets 1,349 leads in a month. Anyone can write "1,349" in a report. Far fewer can open Ads Manager and show you the exact campaign, the exact date range, and the exact number sitting there.

That gap is where most trust in this industry quietly breaks.

For a Tirupur apparel manufacturer, 4,248 wholesale buyer leads came in at ₹16.58 each across six campaigns. Every one of those leads sits in Meta's own lead center, tied to a specific ad and form.

What that habit could not fix: how many of those 4,248 leads became actual orders. That number was never captured, and nothing ever sent it back to Meta to close the loop.

A traceable lead count and a traceable sales outcome are two different disciplines. Most people only build the first one.
